Recently had the opportunity to meet with advocates working to improve the lives of those with Type 1 diabetes. We discussed the importance of research, access to care, and the impact of government policies. Grateful for their work and commitment to improving health outcomes for those affected by T1D.

This morning, I had the pleasure of attending the Southern Lehigh Municipal Update Meeting, where I took questions from community members and talked about how we’re making real investments in securing our communities, funding salary and healthcare for our military service members and veterans, and helping those in need. Hi Veronica, happy to help. Here's the first result from Google showing a recent case during the Biden Administration in which measles swept through a migrant shelter. Unfortunately, as the authors of the report noted, there was "low measles vaccination coverage among shelter residents." This shouldn’t be surprising because immunization rates against measles have plummeted in recent years throughout Latin America and the Caribbean, according to UNICEF. 

Open borders policies like the ones you've supported have allowed millions of illegal immigrants to come into the country, most coming from countries with far lower rates of immunization than we have here in the United States. That lowers our nation's average immunization rate and threatens public health. I hope that helps, and feel free to start working with me to prevent outbreaks like the one in Chicago.

On this National Women's Health Week, we bring awareness to the health challenges impacting women. In the Pennsylvania State House, I was proud to author legislation that created our state's Maternal Mortality Review Committee. In Congress, I'm co-leading the Preventing Maternal Deaths Reauthorization Act of 2025, which enhances funding, strengthens review committees, and supports the dissemination of best practices. I'll keep working to support the fight for women's health.

Political groups and aspiring presidential candidates are working overtime to mislead the public about commonsense government reforms in the new budget. That includes Josh Shapiro, who recently claimed that tens of thousands of local residents would lose SNAP coverage. 

Here’s the truth: SNAP — which is administered by the states with federal dollars — is plagued by waste because of a lack of accountability for errors. For example, Pennsylvania has seen error rates as high as 16% in recent years. This budget makes a commonsense change: when error rates are high, states will pay a portion of the cost. When they’re low, they will continue to pay nothing. It’s up to Governor Shapiro to take accountability for waste, protect taxpayer dollars, and safeguard federal funding.
